newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures end higher on big NYMEX gains.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures end higher on big NYMEX gains.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ended higher on Tuesday after being propelled upward by a surge in NYMEX crude on technical strength, but many traders remained wary of the jump to higher ground.
The May contract settled 75 cents higher at $20.25 a barrel, having hit a low of $19.38 and a high of $20.50 during the session.
Traders attributed the gains to technical strength in NYMEX futures saying a break above $19.25 and then $19.40/45 by the April crude contract had triggered buying by a number of fund-backed players.

Many dealers were cautious of the sharp gains noting that a number of bearish fundamentals still remained such as the overhang of late March North Sea Brent cargoes which has dented physical prices over the past week.
Two late March physical Brents traded at May Brent -70 and -68 on Tuesday, slightly lower than Monday's deals of April -80 and -81 and a few March cargoes were reported to be unsold.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see Brent (futures) being sold into tomorrow, especially if the APIs throw up something bearish," said one trader.

"There's nothing suggesting I should sell just yet," said one technical trader. "But I must admit I would like to see these higher levels done in better volumes." -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
